requirement.summary: KDS2-DEV-03-2-20: Get tickets which within last 24 hours
requirement.description:
Goal

Change GET /api/kds/v1/getTickets so it returns all non-delivered, non-void (active/working) tickets plus delivered and void tickets modified within the last 24 hours, replacing the current fixed “last 50” count limit. Add pagination so clients can fetch large result sets in pages.

Success criteria

- Active/working tickets (statuses other than delivered and void/cancelled) are returned in full — not limited by the 24-hour window or pagination count cap.

- Delivered tickets are included only if ticket.modified >= now - 24 hours.

- Void/cancelled tickets are included only if ticket.modified >= now - 24 hours.

- The fixed limits DELIVERED_TICKET_RETRIEVE_LIMIT (50) and VOID_TICKET_RETRIEVE_LIMIT (50) are removed or replaced by the time filter.

- API accepts pagination params (e.g. page, pageSize) and returns page metadata (e.g. total count, current page, page size).

- Existing clients without pagination params get sensible defaults (e.g. page 0, default page size).

- OpenAPI docs updated to describe the combined result set, time filter, and pagination behavior.

Implementation notes

- Result set composition: Merge three groups:

- All active/working tickets for the display (unchanged behavior).

- Delivered tickets where modified >= now - 24 hours.

- Void/cancelled tickets where modified >= now - 24 hours.

- Primary touchpoints: TicketApiControllerV1, TicketApiServiceImpl, TicketServiceImpl, and TicketEntryRepository queries (findLastXDeliveredTicketIds, findLastXFullyVoidedTicketIds, etc.).

- Time filter: Use Ticket.modified >= Instant.now().minus(24, HOURS) for delivered and void tickets only.

(Note: “modified <= current - 24 hours” would mean older than 24h; for “last 24 hours” the condition should be >=.)

- Replace count-based queries in getTicketEntriesFromLastXDeliveredTicket / getTicketEntriesFromLastXVoidTicket with time-filtered queries; add/use a DB index on (shop_id, modified) if needed for performance.

- Pagination scope: Apply pagination to the combined response (active + recent delivered + recent void), or paginate only delivered/void while always returning all active tickets. Page size is set to 500 by default.

- Response shape: Extend TicketsMessage or wrap it with pagination fields (page, pageSize, totalElements, totalPages).

requirement.summary: IP2COM - Recover USB printing after printer power-off; cleaner service stop; optional auto-restart for long disconnect
requirement.description:
Background

When a USB kitchen printer is powered off while idle, printing may stay unavailable after power-on until the IP2COM service is restarted manually. This change improves automatic recovery and makes service stop release resources cleanly.

What it does

- After USB printer power-off / power-on, reconnects more reliably and can resume printing without a manual service restart

- Speeds reconnect when the USB device is plugged in or powered on again

- Uses shorter reconnect waits at first, then longer waits if the device stays offline (USB only; other device types keep existing behaviour)

- Optional DisconnectWatchdog (off by default): if reconnect keeps failing for a long time, can restart the IP2COM service, with longer waits between restarts overnight so the service is not restarted every few minutes

- Service stop / force-stop closes printers, network connections, and related work properly before exit

- Clearer logs for expected disconnects; less noise when debug is off

- Small HTML printer spacing fix (  handling)

Setup

- New option: disconnect_watchdog under [setup] — leave 0 unless the site needs auto service restart on long disconnect
requirement.release_notes:
Enhancements: [HERO-68252] Recover USB printing after printer power-off; cleaner service stop; optional auto-restart for long disconnect
Descriptions:
IP2COM improves how it handles USB printers that disconnect and come back.
Service stop and restart now release printer and network connections more cleanly.
An optional Disconnect Watchdog can restart the IP2COM service automatically if a device stays disconnected for a long time. It is off by default.
When enabled, early retries are more frequent; if the device stays offline longer, later restarts become much less frequent, so the PC is not disrupted every few minutes.
Still disconnected after an automatic service restart, later restarts wait longer each time (about 5 minutes for the first six, then 30 minutes, 1 hour, 2 hours, 4 hours, and up to 8 hours).
Features:
USB reconnect reliability improvements
USB printers may disconnect or be power-cycled during normal operation.
Due to OS limitations, automatic reconnecting was not always reliable and sometimes required an IP2COM service restart.
This update improves automatic reconnect handling and adds optional recovery for extended disconnects.
Expected behavior
Short USB disconnects
Printer reconnects automatically.
Printing resumes without manual IP2COM restart.
Long USB disconnects
Watchdog disabled: continues retrying reconnect indefinitely.
Watchdog enabled: perform controlled service restarts with progressively longer retry intervals.
Notes for implementation / support:
Applies to USB printers used with IP2COM.
Other printer device types keep their previous reconnect handling and timing.
Setup:
In config.ini, under [setup], add restart_service_on_long_disconnect for on / off the feature
Default: restart_service_on_long_disconnect=0, which keeps Disconnect Watchdog off.
Set restart_service_on_long_disconnect=1 only if the site needs automatic IP2COM service restart after a long reconnect failure.
Existing option restart_service_on_init_error is unchanged and remains separate from Disconnect Watchdog.
Recommendation: keep restart_service_on_long_disconnect=0 for most sites. Turn it on only if a long disconnect still needs a service restart and the site accepts occasional automatic restarts of IP2COM, affecting all devices on that service.

requirement.summary: Android POS App - Apply Goggle Play policy for camera permission, feature declaration, and compliance
requirement.description:
Description

The Android POS application currently has unmanaged camera permission declarations and implementation gaps that risk runtime crashes (SecurityException), unintended Google Play installation restrictions on non-camera hardware, and compliance alignment regarding data safety.

Key Observations

- Implicit Feature Declaration: The app declares <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.CAMERA" /> in the AndroidManifest.xml without an explicit <uses-feature> tag, causing Google Play to implicitly set android:required="true".

- Runtime Permission Handling: Camera APIs may be invoked without robust runtime permission checks, risking a SecurityException on devices running Android 6.0 (API level 23) and higher.

- Data Safety Declaration:

- Collected Camera Frames: The Google Play Data Safety form must accurately reflect how camera frames/photos are handled (e.g., ephemeral local processing for barcode scanning without server upload).

- [Updated 02/09/2026] App Interactions: App interaction data is collected for app functionality.

Technical Impacts

- Installation Restrictions: Devices without a built-in camera are currently blocked from installing the POS app due to the implicit android:required="true" hardware feature requirement.

- App Stability / Crashes: Executing camera operations without checking and requesting runtime permissions leads to unhandled SecurityException crashes.

Follow-Up:

Explicitly Declare Camera Hardware Feature

- Define camera hardware is needed explicitly

Implement Runtime Permission Checks

- Ensure camera permission is validated before invoking any camera intent or hardware API.

- Implement standard permission request flows with graceful denial handling.

Google Play Data Safety & Disclosure Alignment

- [Updated 02/09/2026] App Interactions

- App interaction data is collected for app functionality and is therefore declared as 'Collected' under App Activity > App Interactions in the Play Console.

- Update the Google Play Console Data Safety form accordingly

- Camera Frames

- Confirm and document that camera frames are processed ephemerally on-device (live barcode scanning) and are not persistently stored or transmitted to external servers.

- Update the Google Play Console Data Safety form accordingly.

- [Updated 02/09/2026] The Google Play Console's 'Photos and videos' disclosure applies only to raw image or video file transmissions. Since our Android app processes camera frames locally on-device and only sends the parsed string value to the backend, no media files are collected. Leaving the 'Photos and videos' category undeclared is still remain safe.

-

- References: Understand app privacy & security practices with Google Play's Data safety section - Computer - Google Play Help

requirement.summary: TMS 2.0 - Incorrect change log info after change arrival cover
requirement.description:
Summary

TMS Operation: Change Arrival Cover writes the wrong reservation change log (Table# to [Empty] instead of Arrival Cover from/to).

Steps to Reproduce

- Open TMS Operation.

- Find a reservation that already has a table assigned (e.g. Table 5).

- Mark Host Arrived and set Arrival Cover (e.g. 2). Confirm the reservation is in Host Arrived status.

- Click Arrival again on the same reservation to open Change Arrival Cover.

- Change Arrival Cover from 2 to 4 and click Confirm.

- Open that reservation’s Change Log.

Expected Result

- Arrival Cover is updated successfully.

- Change log records the cover change, e.g. Arrival Cover : from 2 to 4.

- Table number is not logged as changed.

Actual Result

- Arrival Cover is updated, but change log is wrong: Table# : from 5 to [Empty].

- Arrival Cover from/to is not written.

- Cause: updateResvField (field=arrivalGuests) reloads the reservation with tables, then setResvLog compares old tables against empty saveData['TmsResvTable'], so it treats tables as unassigned. resv_arrival_guests was not in $checkResvFields, so Arrival Cover was never logged. The original cover was also overwritten before log write, so even if it were logged, from/to would be the same.

requirement.summary: TMS 2.0 - POS getMembersByConditions fails on SQL Server (GROUP BY memb_id with SELECT *)
requirement.description:
What:

POS / TMS API getMembersByConditions (get_members_by_conditions) throws on SQL Server when the search joins membership (membership no / group no / interface code).

Cake find('all') selects MemMember.* (and belongsTo columns) but GROUP BY is only MemMember.memb_id. SQL Server requires every selected column to be grouped or aggregated (Msg 8120). ORDER BY membership number has the same problem.

MySQL usually passes because ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY is off. Strict MySQL would fail the same way.

GROUP BY is still required: one member can match multiple membership rows, which would duplicate paging rows without it.

Fix:

MemberApiGeneralComponent::getMembersByConditions — page distinct memb_id first (fields + GROUP BY memb_id + recursive -1, ORDER BY MIN(...) for non-id sort columns), then load full guest profiles with memb_id IN (...). POS payload unchanged. Count stays COUNT(DISTINCT memb_id).

After fix:

SQL Server and MySQL both return the same paged member list / full profile as before. Membership-no sort is deterministic (MIN(mmsh_member)) when one member matches multiple memberships.

requirement.summary: TMS 2.0 - MySQL table lock race: two users can lock / assign the same table (lock API + update resv field)
requirement.description:
Summary

On MySQL, two users can lock / assign the same table at the same time (same outlet, date, period).

This is not caused by HERO-67685. Both paths below use the same MySQL table-state write (updateTableState): check then insert, with no exclusive lock. MSSQL already uses sp_getapplock and is out of scope.

HERO-67685 moved Quick Edit Table to server lock on save, so this race on change table is more visible.

Affected paths

- *Lock table API* — floor plan lock / POST table_states (updateTableStates, action lock/block)

- *Update reservation field* — change table via updateResvField → __lockAndUnlockTable

Customer / Environment

- MySQL / Cloud TMS (e.g. Kowloon Shangri-La – Café Kool)

- MSSQL: no change

Steps to Reproduce

- MySQL TMS outlet, two users, same outlet / date / period.

- Path A: both lock the same vacant table at the same time (floor plan or lock table API).

- Path B: two reservations; both change table to the same table at the same time (update_fields).

Current Result

- Both requests can succeed.

- Two lock records can exist for the same table.

- Lock table API: both users can think they hold the lock.

- Update resv field: both reservations can be saved on the same table.

Expected Result

- Second request fails with the existing locked/blocked error.

- Only one lock record for that table.

Proposed Fix

MySQL GET_LOCK only, in TmsTableState::updateTableState (one place → both paths).

- GET_LOCK on outlet + period + date + table + ext (name ≤ 64 chars; timeout 30s, same as MSSQL).

- Success only if return value is 1.

- Under the lock: if table already locked/blocked, fail; else insert. Do not insert a second row.

- Always RELEASE_LOCK in finally (GET_LOCK is not released by commit).

- MSSQL path unchanged.

Do not add UNIQUE index or occupancy check in this ticket.

Acceptance Criteria

- Two concurrent lock table API calls on the same table: one success, one locked/blocked error; one lock row only.

- Two concurrent change-table saves (updateResvField) to the same table: one success, one conflict error.

- MSSQL behaviour unchanged.

Test plan (JMeter)

QA must test concurrency with JMeter, not only two browsers.

Scenarios

- Lock table API — N threads (e.g. 2 / 10 / 20) POST table_states action lock, same outlet / date / period / table, same second (no ramp-up).

- Update resv field — N threads update_fields change table to the same target table on different reservations (or same race as production).

- Repeat for different tables in parallel (no cross-table blocking).

Must pass

- Only *one* winner per table; others return locked/blocked (or existing conflict error). Not two success.

- tms_table_states: *one* lock row for that table key after the burst.

- *No deadlock* (MySQL SHOW ENGINE INNODB STATUS / error log: no deadlock; API must not hang until PHP timeout).

- *No GET_LOCK / InnoDB lock held > 30s* and left in DB:

- After the test, GET_LOCK is released (check performance_schema.metadata_locks / IS_USED_LOCK(name) = 0 / SHOW PROCESSLIST no waiting on named lock).

- GET_LOCK timeout is 30s: waiter either gets the lock within 30s or fails; must not wait forever.

- No leftover tms_table_states lock rows from a request that failed / timed out (failed acquire must not insert; failed request must still RELEASE_LOCK).

- InnoDB row locks from the insert must not remain after the request ends (no trx open > 30s on tms_table_states).

JMeter notes

- Use two (or more) login sessions / tokens.

- Ramp-up 0 for the race; then a soak (e.g. 1–2 min) to catch leaked locks.

- Capture response codes/error keys and a DB snapshot of tms_table_states + IS_USED_LOCK before/after.

Out of Scope

- UNIQUE index / duplicate-row cleanup

- Extra occupancy validation on standard TMS

- HERO-67685 FE lock storm

requirement.description:
User Story

As an MGM compliance and audit stakeholder, I want the Infrasys BI interface to export a new pos_check_extra_infos data file so that we can meet external regulatory and audit reporting requirements.

Current Behavior

The Infrasys BI interface does not currently export a pos_check_extra_infos data file. The pos_check_extra_infos table exists in the database but its data is not included in any BI export. MGM receives the existing set of BI export files only, and there is no mechanism to extract pos_check_extra_infos data for external reporting purposes.

Expected Behavior

The Infrasys BI interface exports a new pos_check_extra_infos data file (e.g., real_pos_check_extra_infos_20260330090841.csv) as a brand-new file added to the existing set of BI export files. Existing files remain unchanged. The file is delivered via SFTP to the same server and directory path used by existing BI export files, on the same daily batch schedule.

The single CSV file contains data from three sections, each with its own filter logic:

ckei_section = 'pms' and ckei_by = 'payment' and coalesce(ckei_status,'') <> 'd'

ckei_section= discount

ckei_variable= member_number、reference

ckei_section=discount_reason

ckei_variable= id

Acceptance Criteria

Export pos_check_extra_infos data file on daily batch schedule

- Given the BI export job runs on its scheduled daily batch

- When the job generates the pos_check_extra_infos export

- Then a single CSV file is produced (e.g., real_pos_check_extra_infos_YYYYMMDDHHMMSS.csv) containing data from all three sections: pms/payment, discount, and discount_reason

- And the file is delivered via SFTP to the same server and directory path as the existing BI export files

- And all existing BI export files are generated and delivered unchanged

- But if no records match the filter criteria for a given batch, an empty file with headers only is still produced and delivered

Apply section-specific row-level filters to exported records

- Given records exist in the pos_check_extra_infos source table

- When the export file is generated

- Then for the pms/payment section, only records where ckei_section = 'pms' AND ckei_by = 'payment' AND ckei_status IS NOT NULL AND ckei_status <> '' AND ckei_status <> 'd' are included

- And for the discount section, only records where ckei_section = 'discount' AND ckei_status IS NOT NULL AND ckei_status <> '' AND ckei_status <> 'd' are included

- And for the discount_reason section, only records where ckei_section = 'discount_reason' AND ckei_status IS NOT NULL AND ckei_status <> '' AND ckei_status <> 'd' are included

- But records with ckei_status IS NULL, ckei_status = '' (empty string), or ckei_status = 'd' are excluded from all sections regardless of ckei_section or ckei_by values

File naming and format consistency

- Given the BI export job completes successfully

- When the pos_check_extra_infos file is written to the export destination

- Then the file name follows the pattern real_pos_check_extra_infos_YYYYMMDDHHMMSS.csv

- And the file uses the same CSV format, encoding, and delimiter conventions as the existing BI export files

- And the file includes a header row with column names matching the variable names from the source data

Alternatives Considered

- Exporting each section (pms/payment, discount, discount_reason) as separate files — rejected in favor of a single combined file per requester confirmation.

- Applying the ckei_section = 'pms' AND ckei_by = 'payment' filter globally to all rows — rejected; the filter is section-specific. Discount and discount_reason sections use only the ckei_status filter (no ckei_section/ckei_by restriction beyond their own section identifiers).

- Modifying an existing BI export file to include this data — rejected; this is a brand-new file to avoid disrupting existing downstream consumers.

- Filtering columns on the pms/payment section — rejected; all columns from the pos_check_extra_infos table are exported for pms/payment records per requester confirmation.

requirement.summary: POS - LPS Debit Card - Mask balances and show "Card is not valid" for invalid cards
requirement.description:
User Story

As a POS user performing an LPS Debit Card enquiry, I want the enquiry result screen to show a standardized "Card is not valid" message and mask balances for invalid cards, so that I am not misled into thinking an invalid card has a usable balance.

Current Behavior

The LPS Debit Card enquiry result screen displays the exact status string returned from the middleware verbatim (e.g., "Freeze", blank). For most non-Normal statuses the card is actually invalid, yet the screen still shows the balance as 0.00, which misleads users into thinking the card has a usable balance.

Expected Behavior

The LPS Debit Card enquiry result screen presents a standardized status display. When the card is valid (status "Normal"), the current display is unchanged. When the card is invalid (status "PendingSales", "isExpired" true, or any other non-Normal status), the screen shows a clear "Card is not valid" message and masks Card Balance, Gift Balance, and Total Balance as ***. When isExpired=true co-occurs with a non-Normal status string, the "Expired (Card is not valid)" message always takes precedence. This is a display-only change: the user can still proceed with any action as before, and all users see the masked balances with no override. Only the LPS Debit Card enquiry result screen is in scope. The Expiry Date is not shown on the enquiry result screen; it appears only in the interface log.

Masking is controlled by a new setup option under Interface Control > LPS Debit Card loyalty interface > General Setup:

- Setup name: Mask Check Value Result Balance

- Dropdown options: No (Default), Yes

- When "Yes", invalid cards show *** balances; when "No" (default), invalid cards show raw balances.

- This option is not available for card status "Normal" (Normal always shows raw balances unchanged).

Acceptance Criteria

Normal status unchanged

- Given the LPS Debit Card enquiry returns status 'Normal'

- When the enquiry result screen is displayed

- Then the current enquiry result display is shown with no modification

Expired card

- Given the LPS Debit Card enquiry returns 'isExpired' as true and the 'Mask Check Value Result Balance' option is 'Yes'

- When the enquiry result screen is displayed

- Then the status shows 'Expired (Card is not valid)' in English or 'Expired (此卡已失效)' in Chinese

- And Card Balance, Gift Balance, and Total Balance display as ***

- But if the returned status is also non-Normal (e.g., 'PendingSales'), the 'Expired (Card is not valid)' message still takes precedence

PendingSales status

- Given the LPS Debit Card enquiry returns status 'PendingSales', 'isExpired' is not true, and the 'Mask Check Value Result Balance' option is 'Yes'

- When the enquiry result screen is displayed

- Then the status shows 'PendingSales (Card is not valid)' in English or 'PendingSales (此卡已失效)' in Chinese

- And Card Balance, Gift Balance, and Total Balance display as ***

Other non-Normal status

- Given the LPS Debit Card enquiry returns a status that is not 'Normal' or 'PendingSales', 'isExpired' is not true, and the 'Mask Check Value Result Balance' option is 'Yes'

- When the enquiry result screen is displayed

- Then the status shows '
{Returned status from interface} (Card is not valid)' in English or '{Returned status from interface}

(此卡已失效)' in Chinese

- And Card Balance, Gift Balance, and Total Balance display as ***

- But if the returned status is blank or empty, the status shows only '(Card is not valid)' in English or '(此卡已失效)' in Chinese with no status name prefix

Masking option set to No

- Given the LPS Debit Card enquiry returns an invalid status (non-Normal) and the 'Mask Check Value Result Balance' option is 'No'

- When the enquiry result screen is displayed

- Then the status message is shown as described for the invalid status

- But Card Balance, Gift Balance, and Total Balance display raw values instead of ***

Supporting Evidence

Reference attachments: Workflow 67356.png. The ticket references example screenshots and interface logs for each status case: "Status - Normal - no change required.png" (Case 1), "Status - PendingSales - change required.png" (Case 2), "IsExpired is true - change required.png" (Case 3), "Other status and not expired - change required.png" (Case 4), plus "Status is Freeze - Invalid.png" and "No status - Invalid.png" (blank/other status examples).

Requested Timeline

Aligned with Priority: Medium

Preferred Quarter: not specified

Target Version: not specified

Notes: no deadline provided by requester

Alternatives Considered

Considered showing the raw status string only versus a standardized "Card is not valid" message; the standardized message was chosen to avoid misleading users. Also considered an override to reveal unmasked balances for troubleshooting, but rejected per requirement that all users see masked balances.

requirement.summary: POS044 Audit Control Listing Report — wrong previous-day date on UTC HQ; optimize loading performance
requirement.description:
Summary / Background

- Report: POS044 — Audit Control Listing Report

- Design: Plugin/Pos/webroot/reports/audit_control_listing/audit_control_listing.rptdesign (MySQL; SQL Server design aligned where applicable)

- This case covers two issues on the same report:

- Date / timezone — auto report “Previous Day” shows the wrong calendar date on UTC HQ.

- Loading performance — main audit-log SQL is slow / appears to hang on large HQ DBs.

Issue 1 — Auto report date incorrect (UTC HQ)

Problem

Auto report email sent on a local morning date (e.g. 2025-01-14 ~06:06) with Date Type = Previous Day (last_bday), but the exported report header and row dates show two calendar days earlier (e.g. 2025-01-12) instead of local yesterday (2025-01-13). Server/DB is UTC.

Root Cause

current_bday / last_bday used bare MySQL CURRENT_DATE() (and BIRT today() for the header). On UTC HQ, local morning can still be the previous UTC calendar day, so “yesterday” is shifted by one extra day. iTimeOffset only shifted the UTC time window of that wrong calendar day; it did not choose the shop-local calendar day first.

Expected

- Previous Day = hotel local yesterday (via iTimeOffset).

- Header date matches the filtered local day.

Fix

- Local today SQL: DATE(DATE_ADD(NOW(), INTERVAL iTimeOffset MINUTE)); last day = that date − 1 day; then apply existing DATE_SUB(..., iTimeOffset) for alog_time UTC bounds.

- Header: localNow = BirtDateTime.addMinute(now, iTimeOffset − JVM offset), then format / addDay(..., -1) for last day.

- Preset must keep a correct iTimeOffset (e.g. UTC+8 → 480).

Issue 2 — Optimize loading performance

Problem

On large HQ databases (very large alog_logs / alog_log_infos), POS044 can run very slowly or appear to hang for a day + multi-outlet selection.

Root Cause

Optimizer often drives from out_outlets and reads alog_logs via outlet_slave (alog_olet_id, alog_slave_id), then applies alog_time as a residual filter (very low filtered). time_outlet (alog_time, alog_olet_id) is not used. Starting from alog_log_infos without a time-first hint makes this worse. Audit Log UI already forces time_outlet for similar queries.

Expected

- Time-first plan on alog_logs for dated listing queries.

- Report completes in a reasonable time on large volumes.

Fix

- Drive from alog_logs with FORCE INDEX (time_outlet), then join infos:

FROM alog_logs FORCE INDEX (time_outlet)
JOIN alog_log_infos ON alog_id = ainf_alog_id
...

- Same pattern as Audit Log LogsController / AuditLogGeneralComponent (forceIndex = 'time_outlet').

- SQL Server design: same join order from alog_logs (no MySQL FORCE INDEX).

References

- Report code: POS044

- Prior custom-report performance path: HERO-39055

- Screenshots on this ticket: auto mail 2025-01-14 vs report date 2025-01-12; parameter = Previous Day

requirement.summary: [Tech] Impact of Changing RabbitMQ createQueue durable from false to true on TMS sendMessageToMQ - Dev
requirement.description:
Changing the durable parameter in createQueue from false to true does not directly alter WebSocket connection behavior or real-time transmission performance.

However, it changes the semantics of whether queues and messages survive broker restarts, which indirectly affects how WebSocket clients experience reconnections and service restarts.

Direct Impact: On the WebSocket Connection Itself

- WebSocket connection establishment, heartbeats, and reconnection logic: These are primarily determined by the client SDK, the server-side WebSocket handling (e.g., Spring WebSocket, STOMP over WebSocket), and the network layer, and are not directly related to whether the queue is durable.

- Real-time latency and throughput: According to RabbitMQ documentation, in most cases, whether a queue is durable does not significantly affect throughput or latency; differences are only noticeable in scenarios with extremely high-frequency queue creation/deletion.

In other words, simply changing an existing queue from non-durable to durable will not cause currently connected WebSocket clients to suddenly become slower or change their connection behavior.

Indirect Impact: Semantic Changes for WebSocket Use Cases

The key difference lies in whether messages persist after restarts and reconnections:

durable = false (Original Setting)

- The queue exists only in memory; after a broker restart, the queue is deleted and all messages inside it are lost.

- Implications for WebSocket clients:

-

- If the client briefly disconnects but the broker does not restart, messages may still remain in the queue (depending on whether you use temporary/auto-delete queues).

-

- Once the broker restarts (deployment, failure, upgrade), all messages buffered in that queue are lost; after reconnection, the client will only receive messages produced after the restart.

- This is more suitable for “real-time state” scenarios, such as:

-

- Real-time notifications, latest chat messages, live dashboard data, where only “current and future” data is needed and historical backfill is not required.

durable = true (New Setting)

- The queue definition is persisted to disk and automatically recreated after a broker restart; if messages are also sent as persistent (delivery mode 2), those messages will be restored after restart.

- Implications for WebSocket clients:

-

- After a broker restart, when a client re-subscribes to the same durable queue, it can continue to receive previously unconsumed persistent messages (provided the messages themselves are persistent and the client has a proper ack mechanism).

-

- If you combine this with STOMP durable subscriptions (e.g., setting durable: true in headers and using a fixed subscription id), clients can receive messages that accumulated while they were offline upon reconnection.

- Suitable for scenarios requiring “at-least-once delivery” or “offline backfill”, such as:

-

- Critical business notifications, order status changes, task result callbacks, which should not be lost due to a broker restart.

Practical Considerations

- Messages must also be persistent

Setting the queue to durable alone is not enough; if messages are still sent as transient (many clients default to transient), messages will still be lost on broker restart.

-

- You need to set deliveryMode = 2 (or the equivalent persistent option in your language) on the publisher side.

- Client ack mechanism must align

To guarantee no message loss, consumers (the backend services feeding WebSocket clients) should ack to RabbitMQ only after confirming the frontend has actually received the message; otherwise, messages may still be lost or duplicated if the service crashes.

- Avoid queue buildup causing WebSocket disconnections or delays

After switching to durable, if clients are offline for long periods or consume slowly, messages can accumulate, potentially leading to:

-

- A large burst of messages on reconnection, causing frontend lag or connection timeouts.

-

- If there is a reverse proxy (e.g., nginx) with proxy buffering enabled, you may see “delayed messages” or “disconnections”; proxy settings may need adjustment.

-

- In practice, temporary WebSocket users are often given auto-delete queues or queues with x-expires so the broker cleans them up automatically.

- Changes in RabbitMQ 4.x

Starting from RabbitMQ 4.0, support for non-exclusive, non-durable queues will be removed; the trend is to encourage the use of durable or quorum queues.

Practical Recommendations (for WebSocket Scenarios)

- For real-time, disposable messages (e.g., live chat, real-time stock ticks):

-

- You can continue using non-durable or temporary queues to reduce disk I/O and the risk of message buildup.
